strategy.summary:
Metallbau Steinfelder KG is a small, sound, owner-led family sheet-metal shop. We are about a tenth of its turnover, and it calls us an important reference customer. It is cooperative, has settled below its ask in every renewal, and held prices flat or cut them while steel rose.

Its costing is a two-year-old spreadsheet, and the owner has offered open-book talks. Real cost drift on its inputs (steel and labour up, power down) is modest but genuine, so we should aim to hold prices roughly flat rather than cut.

Part 330020 (coupling guard) is good quality and well priced, and the rival quoted far higher. Part 330030 (motor bracket) is split with Strasser; Steinfelder is cheaper there but worse on quality, with recurring wrong certificates.

Our chronic late payment is its main legitimate grievance and our cheapest currency.
strategy.decision_maker: The owner personally handles price talks (fast decisions, no approval ladder); inside sales handles day-to-day orders.

other_traits: we are a significant share of its turnover

needs.detail: We pay almost all invoices late on an already short net term; on-time or faster payment matters to a small firm.
It values being our reference supplier and a fair, fact-based relationship.
Rising volume on 330020 and a possible larger quota on 330030 are attractive to it.
A longer, binding commitment helps a small shop plan.
Steel has risen over the last 12 months; once its spreadsheet is updated it may seek relief.

constraints.detail: Its cost basis is two years old and could move either way; our index figures can reset it.
Prices are fixed per calendar year; changes need written notice before the year-end deadline. The framework auto-extends unless notice is given.
No should-cost exists, so margin is unknown. The supplier is healthy and could walk if squeezed.

Take up the owner's open-book offer to settle on facts; flatters his transparency.
Offer our checkable index data to update its stale spreadsheet; frames us as helpful.
Recurring defects on 330030, including wrong certificates; supports ppm and chargeback terms and resists an increase.
Checkable power fall offsets part of any steel claim.
For our internal framing only: it usually settles below its ask, so expect room.
Stable volume; quota shift as a trade.
A fresh fact for a late round, acknowledging the improvement.
Below target but improving; use as a gentle late filler.
Price-notice rule if a late increase request arrives.
Quota can move on 330030; mention calmly, never as a threat.

trades.why: Cash and our late-payment record make faster or reliably on-time payment highly valued; give it as a late-round trade for price.
A 24-month commitment gives planning security for a small shop; offer it early for price stability.
Binding the forecast volume on 330020, or a quota increase on 330030, is valued and within our need.
Fix quality on 330030 without a price premium.
Test the chargeback level rather than give it away; it is currently under-recovered.
Steel is rising, so a clause would pass on the upswing; prefer a fixed price unless the supplier insists.

price_view.reasoning: Cumulative cuts since 2023 roughly match the input decline. Recent steel and labour drift is a few points upward, and the rival is dearer on both parts. The realistic goal is holding current prices, absorbing the drift through terms. Small cuts are possible only if the open book reveals stale overstated costs.

Acknowledge the quality and delivery improvement before raising gaps

Bring checkable figures, not open questions
dont: Threaten to move volume or use deadlines

strategy.writer_notes: Write to the owner in a warm, factual, partnership tone. Recognise the improvement and his offer of transparency, and offer to align on current public indices. Pair every price step with a trade: longer term, binding volume, and on-time or faster payment as the closing trade. Keep a fresh checkable fact for each round, and do not overclaim.

findings.text: No should-cost exists for either part, so the margin above full cost cannot be measured; evidence on room is indirect (index drift, price history, rival quotes). The owner offered to open his calculation (hourly rates, material) – the best route to a real cost view.

Cost drivers point up modestly over 12 months: steel PPI-C241 +6.5% (weight 0.35, about +2.3% on price), labour LCI-C +2.7% (about +0.8% on 330020, +0.7% on 330030), power -3.7% (negligible). Net weighted pressure is about +3.0% on 330020 and +2.8% on 330030. An increase request of around 3% would be index-backed; anything well above is not.

Over the longer run steel is still -6.3% below its 36-month peak (2023-08) and -26.7% below the 2022 high; power -43.5% below its 2022 high. Prices were set in 2023 near peak inputs and have fallen only 7-8% since, so the cumulative input drop roughly matches the cuts already given; neither side has a large structural case. These peak figures are context only, not checkable.

330020: price fell 19.80 (2023) to 18.16 (2026), -8.3%; its new quote 2026-09-26 holds 18.16 flat. The rival Strasser quoted 21.00 in the 2025 benchmark (+15.6% vs current), and Steinfelder won at 20.00 then cut further. Price is already competitive; little room below 18.16 on price evidence alone.

330030: flat at 15.63 since 2024; the 50% split partner Strasser is at 16.11 (+3.1%). In the 2025 RFQ Steinfelder quoted 16.70, above its own running price, yet lost to Strasser's 16.90 award. Steinfelder is the cheaper of two sources; quality on this part is weaker (8 complaints, one 8D open), which is the better lever than price.

Owner costs from a spreadsheet last updated two years ago; it may underestimate recent steel rises but also still carry 2024 power/steel levels. Historically settles 2-3 pp below its ask and did not raise prices in the last renewals despite steel rising.

Supplier is small (2-5 M EUR) and we are ~11% of turnover; equity 33%, stable credit. Pushing below cost risks health; realistic target is holding prices flat (absorbing the ~3% drift) rather than cuts.

findings.text: Owner-led family KG (40 staff, turnover 2-5 M EUR): the owner personally handles price talks. He is open and cooperative and offered to walk us through his calculation (hourly rates, material). Decisions are likely fast with no approval ladder. A routine contact change moved day-to-day sales to inside sales in Oct 2025.

Stale costing: the owner works from his own spreadsheet, last updated two years ago, and asked where our index figures come from. His cost claims may be off in either direction. 2024 steel sat near the 36-month peak, so an old basis may overstate his material cost. However, the 12-month steel index is +6.5% (about +2.3% on price), so he may also discover a real rise. Taking up his calculation offer lets us anchor on facts.
We matter to them. We are about 11% of their turnover, and they called Hollerau an important reference customer at the 2026 supplier day. Recognition and the relationship carry weight with them.
Financially sound and stable: equity ratio 33%, credit index 230 unchanged over 12 months, audit grade A. There is no distress, so they can afford to walk away; they are not desperate.

Our payment behaviour is a sore point. We pay 95.7% of invoices late, 9.6 days after due on average, max 23 days, on a 30-day net term. For a small firm this costs real cash. They have legitimate grounds to complain and to ask for faster payment; paying on time is a cheap concession we can offer.
Accommodating history: prices on both parts have fallen since 2023, and renewals settle well below their ask. They are a soft negotiator but may feel squeezed now.
Evidence on persona is thin: four short notes, no news and no complaint letters.

findings.text: Framework agreement ctr:4600070340 covers both parts (330020 coupling guard, 330030 motor bracket HB), runs 2025-07-01 to 2027-06-30 and auto-extends 12 months unless terminated with 90 days' notice (by 2027-04-01). Prices are fixed per calendar year; any change needs written notice at least 90 days before year end, i.e. by ~2026-10-02 for 2027. A price request arriving after that date has no contractual basis for 2027.

Terms: payment 30 days net (our standard is 60, so this is already a concession to them), DAP, 21-day lead time, quality agreement with 95% OTD target and EUR 150 flat fee per supplier-caused complaint. OTD is 88.5%, below target. Only EUR 900 has been recharged for 8 complaints on 330030 and nothing for 2 on 330020.

History: in every renewal they settled below their ask. On 330020: asked -3.2/+0.4/+0.2, settled -6.1/-1.1/-1.3, a gap of about 2 pp. On 330030: asked -3.4/+2.1/+3.2, settled -7.4/0/0, a gap of about 3 pp. The last two 330030 increase requests were fully rejected. Prices are down 8.3% and 7.4% since 2023.

Sourcing: we own the tooling for both parts. On 330030 they hold only a 50% quota; Strasser holds the other 50%, is active, won the 2025 benchmark and is paid 16.11 vs 15.63, so it is dearer. On 330020 they hold 100%; Strasser is qualified but has 0% quota and quoted 21.00 in the 2025 RFQ, 15.6% above. A move is therefore feasible but costly on 330020.

Dependency: our spend is about EUR 387k, roughly 11% of their turnover, and they call us an important reference customer. They are a small family KG with sound finances (equity 33%, stable credit index). The owner is open to sharing his calculation but uses an index spreadsheet that is two years out of date. The 12-month steel index has risen (+6.5%), which supports a modest increase request.

Faster or on-time payment (we pay 9.6 days late on average)

findings.text: Delivery is below the 95% contract target but improving and above peers: rolling 12m OTD 88.5% vs requested (90.4% vs confirmed), up from 85.7% a year earlier; peers' median 84.6%. Lateness has shortened (avg 7.7 days late, max 11 in last 12m vs 11.3/25 overall). Note the KNOWN_ISSUES caveat on requested vs confirmed dates.

Quality peaked at 849 ppm (2025Q3, class B amber) and has fallen steadily to 489 ppm (2026Q3, class A green, 0 overdue 8D), but is still above the peers' median of 457 ppm. Recovery is real, so attacking overall quality is weak; supplier can use the trend in its favour.

Part 330030 (motor bracket) is the problem part: 8 supplier-caused QNs in last 12m, recurring 'wrong material certificate' (4 since 2025-03) plus burrs, leakage, dimension. It runs about 870 ppm vs about 225 ppm on 330020, and 14.8% late deliveries vs 8% on 330020. The second source sup:70360 runs 762 ppm on the same part at a 50% quota, so Steinfelder is the worse of the two on quality. It is cheaper, though (15.63 vs 16.11).
Part 330020 (coupling guard) is in good shape: 92% on time, 2 supplier-caused QNs in last 12m, 100% quota with Steinfelder. The latest QN qn:20005002 is not supplier-caused.

Complaint fees are low and inconsistently charged: many supplier-caused QNs show EUR 0 recharged despite the EUR 150 flat fee. The defect cost to us is under-recovered, which supports a chargeback or ppm term rather than a price argument.

Volume outlook rises for 330020 and holds for 330030. The 330020 forecast is 15,040 pcs vs 13,300 ordered last 12m (+13%). The 330030 total forecast is 18,790 vs 18,360, of which Steinfelder gets about half. Forecasts are shared with the supplier and have been stable, so they can be offered credibly as volume commitment in exchange for price or terms.
Price history is supplier-friendly: prices fell 8.3% (330020) and 7.4% (330030) since 2023. The current anchors are 18.16 and 15.63, both stable through 2026.

arguments.text: We have cut or held prices every year since 2023 (330020 -8.3 % cumulative, 330030 -7.4 %) while steel and labour rose; there is nothing left to give, the drift now runs against us.

Input costs: steel +6.5 % in 12 months (about a third of our cost), labour +2.7 % (about 25-31 %); together roughly +3 % on the part cost, partly offset by power, which is a small share. Our 18.16 offer is already a hold, not an increase.
We are the cheaper source: Strasser quoted 21.00 vs our 20.00 on 330020 and charges 16.11 vs our 15.63 on 330030, and its lead time is longer.
Hollerau pays late: 95.7 % of invoices late, on average 9.6 days in the last 12 months, max 23, on a 30-day term. That is unpaid financing we carry for a small family firm.
330020 delivers well: 92 % on time in the last 12 months and 225 ppm. Overall OTD is improving and the scorecard is back to green, 91.8.
The contract fixes prices per calendar year and runs to mid-2027. Any change needs 90 days' notice, so a mid-year cut has no basis.
Open book offered: we are ready to show hourly rates and material, which shows good faith.

weak_points: 330030 quality: 870 ppm, recurring wrong material certificates (4 since Mar 2025), leakage, burrs; worse than Strasser's 762 ppm.
330030 OTD only 85.2 % in the last 12 months; the 95 % contract target is missed on both parts.
Our costing spreadsheet is two years old; the open book could reveal overstated or stale figures.
We said Hollerau is an important reference customer, about 10 % of turnover, so we depend on them.
Steel is still -6.3 % below its 36-month peak and -26.7 % below its 2022 high, while our prices are only about 8 % below 2023.
Strasser is qualified on 330020 and active at 50 % on 330030, so the customer has an alternative.
We lost the 2025 benchmark RFQ on 330030 even though our price was lower.
wants: Payment that is actually on time, or faster (e.g. 14-20 days), in exchange for holding prices.
A larger 330030 quota (e.g. 60-70 %) or a binding annual volume.
A steel index clause if we are asked to cut, or else fixed prices with a small premium.
red_lines: No price cut below the current 18.16 / 15.63 without volume or payment compensation.
No reduction greater than about 1 % even with all trades.
No higher chargeback per complaint or a ppm penalty we cannot meet on 330030 before the certificate process is fixed.
No mid-year price change outside clause 3.1.
red_team.opening: Thank them for the partnership; note we have held 330020 at 18.16 and 330030 at 15.63 despite steel +6.5 % and labour +2.7 %. Propose prices unchanged for 2027, conditional on payment strictly at 30 days (or faster) and a longer term. Offer the open-book walkthrough and a concrete 8D action on 330030 certificates, and ask for a quota increase on 330030 in return.

rebuttals.answer: You are right that your prices have come down since the first orders, and we value that. But those reductions followed an earlier high point in material costs, so they largely passed on lower inputs rather than giving away margin. Our aim is not a deep cut. We want a stable price that both sides can defend on current facts, and we will reward that with planning security.

We agree that steel and labour have moved up, and the public indices confirm it. Weighted by their share of the part, the effect is moderate. Power has fallen and offsets a small part of it. We welcome that your new offer holds the coupling guard price. We suggest aligning both parts on the same current public sources, since your spreadsheet has not been refreshed for some time.

Price is one part of the picture, and your competitiveness on the coupling guard is one reason the volume there is growing. On the motor bracket we look at total cost, and quality and delivery weigh heavily there. The complaint record on that part currently works against you. A competitive price is what keeps the larger share in reach.

This is a fair point and we will not dispute it. Paying you reliably on time is something we can commit to. We are also open to discussing faster payment as part of an overall agreement, because we understand what it means for a family business.

We acknowledge the clear improvement on the coupling guard and in the overall scorecard, and we are glad to see it. On-time delivery is still below the agreed target on both parts, however. The motor bracket in particular lags on delivery and on complaints. We would like to build on the progress with a quality commitment there.

We fully respect the contract. Prices are fixed per calendar year, and the same notice rule applies to any change in either direction. We are discussing the coming year's prices within that framework. The framework also leaves both sides free to review it at its term, so a fair agreement now serves us both.

We appreciate this offer very much and gladly accept it. Looking at hourly rates and material together, against current public indices, is the fairest way to settle prices that last. We will bring our index sources to make the comparison easy.

press: Could we together look at what is behind the recurring wrong material certificates and the leakage findings on the motor bracket, and agree a quality target that avoids them?
We would welcome a plan to bring on-time delivery on the motor bracket up to the agreed target, since that is what we weigh most when deciding the share of that part.
When we go through your calculation, could we update the material and labour figures to current public indices so that both of us work from the same, fresh basis?
As you kindly called us an important reference customer, we would like to reflect that partnership in a longer commitment and growing volume, paired with stable prices.
A larger share of the motor bracket is open to the supplier that combines a competitive price with reliable quality, and we would be glad if that were you.
